hero.headline: The machine warns you before it stops.
hero.subline: RASD is a condition-monitoring system that learns the normal operating signature of every machine on your line, then alerts you when its behaviour begins to change — while there is still time to plan the repair instead of being caught by the stoppage.

cost.heading: An unplanned stop costs more than the part that failed.
cost.body: When a machine stops without warning, the damage does not end with the fault. The shift stops with it, and everything that depends on the shift: idle labour, spare parts on emergency freight, orders that miss their date. The same fault, caught early, is handled in scheduled downtime, with a part ordered calmly and a crew ready. The difference between the two outcomes is not the fault — it is when you learned about it.

stages.title: Day zero — the machine in its normal state
stages.body: The machine runs inside its usual range. At this stage the system watches and learns its particular rhythm: how it vibrates, how it warms, how its current behaves in ordinary operation.

stages.title: First drift — nobody can hear it yet
stages.body: A small mechanical flaw in a bearing begins to change the vibration signature slightly. No excess heat, no unusual noise, nothing a routine walk-around would catch. The system notices the difference because it knows what this machine looks like when it is healthy.

stages.title: The drift confirms — the alert goes out
stages.body: Readings outside the normal range keep recurring, and other channels begin to confirm them. At that point the system does more than notice a difference: it sends the supervisor an alert naming the machine and the indicator that changed.

stages.title: The stoppage that never happened
stages.body: The affected part is replaced in the next scheduled maintenance stop. No lost shift, no emergency freight, no improvised decision in the middle of production. That is the value RASD delivers: the time between the first signal and the actual stop.

warningWindow.closing: In reliability engineering this interval is called the P‑F interval. Its length depends on the type of fault, the machine and its operating conditions; it can range from days to months.

sensors.name: Vibration
sensors.body: The earliest channel for detecting change. A fault begins mechanically, so its effect shows in a machine's vibration before it produces heat or noise anyone can hear. Following this channel is what gives your team a window in which to act.

sensors.name: Temperature
sensors.body: An indicator that confirms what vibration has seen. Temperature rises as a fault develops and friction increases, so it arrives later than vibration — but it raises confidence in an alert when the two move together.

sensors.name: Electrical current
sensors.body: Reveals what vibration cannot: faults that begin inside the electric motor itself. Each fault type shows up first in a different channel, which is why RASD reads all three together.

baseline.heading: There is no single “normal” for all machines.
baseline.body: Even two machines of the same model in the same plant do not behave alike; mounting, foundation, load and operating age leave a different signature on each. So RASD does not rely on a general table or a ready-made limit. It begins with a learning period on your machine while it is running healthy, builds a reference of its own from that, and measures every later reading against that reference alone.
baseline.callout: One condition cannot be waived: the machine must be healthy when learning begins. The system learns the machine as it finds it — if it learns a faulty machine, it treats the fault as part of its character. That is why we verify its condition first.

deliverables.title: An alert on the supervisor's phone
deliverables.body: A direct message naming the machine, the indicator that changed and since when, delivered to the person who can act on it. No dashboard someone has to open to discover the problem.

deliverables.title: A record that grows more valuable with time
deliverables.body: Each machine's readings are kept, so over the months you build a real history of how it behaves. That record helps your maintenance team understand its equipment, and becomes the foundation for any later improvement in alert accuracy.

deliverables.title: Installation without touching the machine
deliverables.body: Sensors mount externally — no cut wiring, no opened housings, no modification to the machine itself. Installation is scheduled around your production plan.

limits.heading: The limits of this system, stated plainly.
limits.body: No predictive-maintenance system detects every fault without a single false alarm. That is not a question of product quality but of the problem itself: any system that decides when to alert balances an alarm that was not needed against a fault that went unseen, and tightening one loosens the other. So we do not promise what cannot be delivered. We commit to telling you, before any agreement, what RASD can and cannot detect on your specific machine, and what an early warning is likely to look like on it.

installation.title: Visit and assess
installation.body: We visit the site, assess your lines, identify the machines whose stoppage costs you most, and agree the mounting points with you.

installation.title: Mount the sensors
installation.body: Sensors are fitted externally on the selected machines, in a way that suits your production schedule.

installation.title: The learning period
installation.body: The system records the machine in ordinary operation and builds its own reference, with no change to your daily work.

installation.title: Switch on alerting
installation.body: RASD begins comparing readings and sending alerts, and we review the first results with you to tune sensitivity to your plant.

closing.heading: Start with one machine.
closing.body: Pick the machine whose stoppage costs you most, put the system on it, and judge the result yourself after a real period of operation.
